title: The Parable of the Talents
text:
Jesus told of a man who was going on a long journey. Before he left, he called his servants and entrusted his property to them. To one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one, each according to his ability. A talent was a very large sum of money, worth many years of a laborer's wages.

The servant with five talents went at once and traded with them and made five more. The one with two did the same and gained two more. But the one who had received one talent dug a hole in the ground and hid his master's money.

After a long time the master returned and settled accounts. The first two servants brought their gains, and to each he said: "Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a little; I will set you over much."

Then the third came. "Master," he said, "I knew you to be a hard man, reaping where you did not sow. So I was afraid, and I went and hid your talent in the ground. Here is what is yours." The master called him wicked and lazy. If that was what he believed, he should at least have put the money with the bankers, so it would have earned interest. He had the talent taken from him and given to the servant who had ten, and the useless servant was thrown out.
lesson: When you are trusted with resources, doing nothing out of fear is also a choice, and usually a poor one. Put what you have been given to work and own the risk.
